title: [spec-gap][R-LOADNG-004/020] Originate-side RREQ_RATELIMIT 10/min absent in all stacks; B2.7 broadcast-limit interaction unwirable
description:
Spec B2.1: RREQ_RATELIMIT 10/min 'Max RREQs originated per minute'. B2.7: RREQ flooding is subject to the same broadcast rate limits as other mesh-wide traffic (05-routing 6.3.3), and RREQ_RATELIMIT is an additional per-node limit on originated RREQs. Classification: not-implemented.

Evidence: no originate-side RREQ limiter exists in any stack. The only RREQ rate limiter is C's receive-side admission control (10/min per source + 30/min global, implementing 05-routing 10.3 — a different requirement from B2.1): lichen/subsys/lichen/routing/loadng.c:41-56,453-492, tested by test_rreq_rate_limit_per_source/global/window_expiry (lichen/tests/loadng/main.c:575-630). Python and Rust have no RREQ rate limiting; python rreq_jitter only staggers TX. Because no stack drives RREQ origination in production (see unwired-discovery beads b7z9.195/.196/.197), the B2.7 interaction cannot currently be exercised.

Suggested placement: per-node originate limiter inside each discovery driver (python node.py driver, rust hybrid.rs, C adapter), plus a test that originated RREQs respect both the 6.3.3 broadcast budget and B2.1 10/min.
